the rear gate on the north wall - research/questions/0101-privies-setchin.html: a samurai residence had a rear wicket or gate, the fujomon, for carrying out night soil, the dead and criminals (three Japanese dictionaries; no residence named, no size given), so a lesser gate at the rear of the household's court, onto the rear yard, lets the night-soil collector reach the house's privies without crossing the public court (building-review 2026-11-22 O3, 449 T326); drawn as a one-bay rear gate of 6 ft, inside the side gate's 5-8 ft band (docs/buildings.md; size-audit 2026-11-22), not a kugurido wicket of about 2.5-3 ft, which the gate floor of 5 ft refuses (449 T340); its seat, and the collector's way through no kitchen or service court, a GUESS
